newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: W&H says well placed for growth.
newsitem.headline: W&H says well placed for growth.

text.p: Publisher Wilson and Horton Ltd, 85 percent owned by Independent Newspapers Plc, said on Monday it was well placed for further growth when business confidence returned to the New Zealand market.
Wilson and Horton reported a net profit of NZ$21.3 million for the six months to June 30, up 17.1 percent on last year's first half net of $18.19 million.
"With a strong cost containment policy in operation the group should move strongly ahead as business confidence returns to the marketplace," Wilson and Horton said in a statement.
"The directors believe the results show that the company has adapted well to the slower economy of recent years."
Sales for the period increased 1.8 percent to $216.4 million and operating earnings before interest and tax increased 6.9 percent to $42.4 million.
"The continuing lack of confidence by businesses and consumers is reflected in the small increase in revenue for the period under review," the company said.

"Nevertheless, the overall result is a most satisfactory one, with the increase in operating earnings coming not just from the New Zealand Herald (newspaper) but from improved performances from some of the group's other publishing businesses."
